item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Three material outcome-scope decisions remain: the deployment trust boundary, which objects collaboration exposes, and whether cross-deployment federation is an explicit non-goal.","questions":[{"decision_key":"deployment_tenancy_trust_boundary","label":"Deployment trust boundary","context":"A tenant is a separately administered group whose users and data must be isolated from other groups. NexusCentral already targets multiple concurrent users on one deployment, but the intended trust boundary is not fixed.","evidence":"`services/nexus-node/src/nexus-node.mjs` is one durable host authority, while `adapters/runtime-adapters/src/sqlite-store.mjs` stores canonical snapshots, events, and host values in one SQLite boundary. This supports concurrent users today but does not establish isolation between unrelated organizations.","impact":"This decides whether authentication, authorization, persistence, secrets, audit records, and backup design can assume one collaborating team or must enforce organization-grade isolation. It is a foundational security and data-model choice that will be expensive to reverse.","question":"Who may safely share one production NexusCentral deployment?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"One trusted team","consequence":"Immediately support multiple named users with per-user ownership and explicit sharing inside one trusted organization; long term, keep deployment-per-team as the isolation boundary and avoid multi-tenant complexity."},{"number":2,"text":"Multiple isolated organizations","consequence":"Immediately require tenant-scoped identities, storage, credentials, quotas, audits, and administration; long term, enable hosted or shared infrastructure at substantially higher security and migration cost."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"The stated product centers on collaborating technical operators using one deployment. Treating that deployment as one trusted-team boundary satisfies the requirement while preserving a clear path to add stronger tenancy later.","priority":97},{"decision_key":"collaboration_visibility_scope","label":"Collaboration visibility","context":"A shared object is a conversation, workflow definition, run, or artifact that another authorized user can view or act on. Work memory is already isolated per conversation, so collaboration needs an explicit sharing rule.","evidence":"`apps/web/app/page.jsx` will become the six-tab Work, Router, Models, Workflows, Runs, and Settings surface. The verified product boundary says Work owns per-conversation memory, while Workflows and Runs own reusable definitions and immutable execution evidence.","impact":"This determines the permissions model, default navigation, search visibility, audit events, and whether private conversational context can leak into team workflows. Long term, it defines whether NexusCentral feels like a private operator tool with collaboration or a shared workspace by default.","question":"Which NexusCentral objects should collaborators see by default?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Private Work, shared operations","consequence":"Keep Work conversations private unless explicitly shared, while published workflows and authorized run evidence are team-visible; long term, preserve personal context boundaries without weakening operational collaboration."},{"number":2,"text":"Everything explicitly shared","consequence":"Make conversations, workflows, runs, and artifacts private until their owner shares them; long term, maximize control but add permission friction to routine team operations."},{"number":3,"text":"Team-visible by default","consequence":"Expose conversations, workflows, runs, and artifacts to the trusted team unless marked private; long term, simplify discovery but increase accidental context disclosure and ownership ambiguity."},{"number":4,"text":"Conversations never shared","consequence":"Keep Work conversations permanently private and allow collaboration only through workflows, runs, and promoted records; long term, create the strongest boundary but prevent direct conversational handoff."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"Private conversations with shared operational records matches per-conversation memory isolation and gives collaborators the durable evidence they need without exposing raw operator context automatically.","priority":94},{"decision_key":"cross_deployment_federation_scope","label":"Deployment federation","context":"Federation means two independent NexusCentral deployments sharing authority over workflows, queues, users, or canonical run state. Provider connections are different: they only supply execution capacity to one authority.","evidence":"`services/nexus-node/src/nexus-node.mjs` defines one durable host authority, and `docs/14-PROVIDERS-AND-PEERJS-ROOMS.md` keeps LAN and PeerJS transport separate from provider and routing authority. Nothing verified establishes shared canonical authority between NexusCentral deployments.","impact":"This decides whether the plan can preserve one canonical database and coordinator or must add distributed identity, conflict resolution, replication, and cross-host recovery. Making federation a launch goal would reshape nearly every domain boundary.","question":"Should coordination between separate NexusCentral deployments be part of the production outcome?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"No, explicit non-goal","consequence":"Each deployment remains the sole authority for its users, workflows, and runs while remote providers contribute execution only; long term, retain simple crash recovery and add federation later through a new contract if justified."},{"number":2,"text":"Read-only exchange","consequence":"Allow deployments to export or subscribe to workflows and evidence without sharing live authority; long term, support organizational exchange with manageable provenance and versioning complexity."},{"number":3,"text":"Full federation","consequence":"Allow deployments to coordinate live queues, workflows, approvals, and canonical state; long term, enable distributed organizations but require consensus, replication, identity federation, and conflict recovery now."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"The verified architecture deliberately concentrates authority in one durable host while treating LAN and PeerJS peers as providers. Keeping federation out of scope protects that reliability model and still permits multi-user collaboration within each deployment.","priority":90}]}
